stories.title: Law Firm Dunn Isaacson Rhee Establishes NYC Office at 7 World Trade Center
stories.excerpt: Silverstein Properties announced that Dunn Isaacson Rhee LLP has signed a new lease for 11,167 square feet of office space on the 34th floor of 7 World Trade Center. The lease establishes a New York office for the firm, an elite litigation boutique.“Dunn Isaacson Rhee represents the caliber of organization that continues to define 7 World Trade Center as one of Downtown Manhattan’s premier office destinations,” said Keith Cody, Head of Commercial Leasing at Silverstein Properties. “Today’s leading firms are seeking workplaces that reflect their brand, support their people, and provide an exceptional experience for their clients. Through thoughtful design, hospitality-driven amenities, and a commitment to excellence, 7 World Trade Center continues to deliver an environment that meets those expectations.”Tenant representation was provided by Lisa Ann Pollakowski, Cory Gahr and Richard Plehn of Lee & Associates. Ownership was represented in-house by Cody, Gordon Hough, and Harlan Strader, with CBRE agency leasing support from MaryAnn Tighe and team. The post Law Firm Dunn Isaacson Rhee Establishes NYC Office at 7 World Trade Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Dunn Isaacson Rhee LLP leases 11,167 SF at 7 World Trade Center, Downtown Manhattan
Law firm office demand signals financial district recovery post-pandemic
Silverstein Properties continues filling premium office space in Lower Manhattan
stories.summary: Dunn Isaacson Rhee, an elite litigation boutique, signed an 11,167-square-foot lease on the 34th floor of 7 World Trade Center in Lower Manhattan. The lease represents continued office tenant demand at Silverstein Properties' flagship Downtown Manhattan asset. This signals ongoing recovery in the post-pandemic office market, particularly for premium, branded workspaces.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Office leasing strength in Downtown Manhattan indicates white-collar job stability, which supports residential demand indirectly, but the effect is modest and already-priced into Manhattan multifamily fundamentals.

stories.title: Newmark Closes Note Sale on San Pedro Adaptive Reuse
stories.excerpt: Newmark arranged the sale of a note secured by Topaz Tower, a fully entitled adaptive reuse development project located at 222 W. 6th St. in San Pedro. The 12-story, 309,732-square-foot office tower is entitled for conversion to 246 market-rate multifamily units. Executive Managing Director Ryan Plummer, Co-Head of U.S. Capital Markets Kevin Shannon, Vice Chairman Ken White, Senior Managing Director Chris Benton and Managing Director Anthony Muhlstein represented the lender. The buyer was 222 PV Harbor View, LLC, a private Los Angeles-based residential developer. “Topaz Tower represents an exceptionally rare opportunity to acquire a fully entitled coastal high-rise multifamily conversion with scale, ocean views and an immediate execution path in a rapidly evolving submarket,” said Plummer. Topaz Tower Apartments will include a mix of studio, one-, two- and three-bedroom residences with an average unit size of 835 square feet. Planned amenities include a rooftop deck with a resort-style pool, ocean-view units, balconies and high ceilings. The post Newmark Closes Note Sale on San Pedro Adaptive Reuse appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Topaz Tower, San Pedro: 246-unit fully entitled adaptive reuse, 12-story, 309K SF
Private LA developer 222 PV Harbor View acquired note; coastal high-rise with scale and ocean views
San Pedro submarket rapidly evolving; adaptive reuse conversions attract capital as rare entitled supply
stories.summary: Newmark closed a note sale on Topaz Tower, a fully entitled adaptive reuse project in San Pedro converting a 12-story office tower into 246 market-rate multifamily units with an average unit size of 835 square feet. The buyer was 222 PV Harbor View LLC, a private Los Angeles residential developer. The deal signals strong appetite for entitled coastal multifamily conversions in rapidly evolving Los Angeles submarkets.
stories.impact: San Pedro's adaptive reuse pipeline is attracting residential capital and showcasing a path to dense, coastal supply in a supply-constrained market. As the submarket evolves (per the deal description), competition for entitled conversions will intensify; developers with land in adjacent submarkets should monitor San Pedro's absorption and rent growth to calibrate timing of their own coastal or near-coastal projects in LA.

stories.title: Venture X Coworking Location to Open in Pompano Beach
stories.excerpt: Priddy Spaces has signed a 20,000-square-foot lease for a Venture X coworking location in Pompano Beach, Fla. The coworking operator signed a 10-year lease at a 44,102-square-foot office property within Grover Corlew’s Mayla Pompano mixed-use development. Located at 2335 East Atlantic Boulevard, the four-story office building sits two blocks east of Dixie Highway and was constructed in 2020. The coworking outpost — which will span the building’s second, third and fourth floors — will feature 85 private office suites and four meeting rooms. It’s expected to open next year. “Pompano Beach is experiencing one of the most exciting transformations in South Florida,” Kevin Priddy, co-founder and CEO of Priddy Spaces, said in a statement. “The combination of new residential development, improved infrastructure, vibrant dining and retail, and its proximity to the beach has created an environment where businesses and talent want to be.” Pompano Beach, long a working-class town, is seeing a rush of luxury condo development along its coast, from the likes of Miami-based Related Group and other developers. West Palm Beach-based Priddy Spaces is a franchisee of Venture X, operating five locations in South Florida, with Vast Coworking Group serving as the franchisor. Private equity firm New State Capital Partners purchased Vast Coworking Group earlier this year for an undisclosed amount. Priddy Spaces operates a Venture X location in nearby Boca Raton at Grover Corlew’s Palmetto Central office campus. The four-acre Mayla Pompano mixed-use development includes a 355-unit apartment building and two other office properties. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Venture X signs 20K SF, 10-year lease in Pompano Beach mixed-use development
Coworking expansion reflects Pompano Beach transformation: new residential, infrastructure, dining, retail
Grover Corlew's Mayla development anchors mixed-use growth along Atlantic Boulevard
stories.summary: Priddy Spaces signed a 10-year, 20,000-square-foot lease for a Venture X coworking location at Grover Corlew's Mayla Pompano mixed-use development. The coworking space will occupy the second, third, and fourth floors of a 2020-built office building on East Atlantic Boulevard and is expected to open in 2025. The lease reflects Pompano Beach's rapid transformation from a working-class town into a destination attracting businesses and talent via new residential, dining, retail, and beach proximity.
stories.impact: Coworking expansion and business-class amenity growth in Pompano Beach signals rising white-collar and service-class job demand in South Florida, which will drive rental absorption across income tiers in the submarket. Multifamily developers should view Pompano Beach as an emerging micro-market with infrastructure and lifestyle momentum; first-mover advantage in Class A rental apartments near Atlantic Boulevard and waterfront precincts could capture in-migration before rents spike.

stories.title: Domain Lines Up $176M Financing for Mixed-Income Astoria Rentals
stories.excerpt: The Domain Companies has closed on $175.6 million in financing with Wells Fargo for a new mixed-income housing project called Elara, which will deliver 429 new apartments in Astoria, Queens. Domain’s equity partners on the deal are Canyon Partners Real Estate and BLDG Management. The financing was brokered by Chris Peck and Nicco Lupo of JLL Capital Markets. “Astoria is one of New York’s most vibrant and culturally rich neighborhoods, and it has long held a special place in Domain’s history,” said Matt Schwartz, co-CEO of Domain Companies.“We’re proud to deepen that connection by delivering a thoughtfully designed residential community that reflects the character of the neighborhood while offering one of the highest-quality living experiences in the market.” The project includes an 18-story building with 330 apartments called Elara East, and a 12-story building with 99 apartments named Elara West. The development includes 107 permanently affordable homes. The buildings are located at 35-45, 35-33 and 35-42 41st St, with Elara West anticipated to open in February 2028, and Elara East expected in September 2028. The post Domain Lines Up $176M Financing for Mixed-Income Astoria Rentals appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Domain Companies closes $175.6M financing (Wells Fargo) for Elara, 429 units in Astoria, Queens
Mixed-income: 107 permanently affordable homes among 330 units (East) + 99 units (West)
Two-tower development, Q2 2028 and Q3 2028 deliveries; equity partners: Canyon Partners, BLDG Management
stories.summary: Domain Companies secured $175.6 million in construction financing from Wells Fargo for Elara, a 429-unit mixed-income rental project in Astoria, Queens. The development comprises two buildings—Elara East (330 units, 18 stories) and Elara West (99 units, 12 stories)—with 107 permanently affordable units. Elara West is expected to deliver in February 2028 and Elara East in September 2028. JLL Capital Markets brokered the financing; equity partners are Canyon Partners Real Estate and BLDG Management.
stories.impact: Large, stabilized construction financing with a quasi-public equity co-investor signals confidence in Astoria's rental fundamentals and acceptance of mixed-income underwriting by marquee lenders. Astoria has been a magnet for in-migration and young professional households; Domain's scale and permanent affordability commitment suggest the submarket can support both market-rate and subsidized supply. Competitors should monitor Astoria absorption and rent trajectory post-2028 to gauge whether mixed-income projects canScale; if successful, it could unlock land sites held by non-profits or institutions seeking mixed-income conversion partners.

stories.title: La La Land Cafe Signs with Brixton Capital for First San Diego Location
stories.excerpt: Brixton Capital, a vertically integrated owner and operator of retail and multifamily properties, has secured a lease with La La Land Café to occupy the mezzanine terrace and café space at its upscale Del Mar Plaza retail destination. La La Land will occupy 1,168 square feet of interior space, with additional sitting and queueing space extending onto the terrace deck. The construction start and grand opening dates are not yet determined. The space was formerly occupied by Pacifica Breeze Café. “We’re proud to be first-to-market attracting a dynamic brand that has grown to over 30 locations since its founding in 2019,” said Brixton Capital founder and chairman Marc Brutten. “We expect the grand opening will be very well attended, and that La La Land Café at Del Mar Plaza will remain a very popular social destination.” Victoria Pappas, Brittney Austin and Linda Rubiola of SHOP Companies represented La La Land, while Brixton Capital represented itself, with support from Andrew Shemirani and Ashley Tiefel at Urban Property Group. Lease terms were not disclosed. The post La La Land Cafe Signs with Brixton Capital for First San Diego Location appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: La La Land Café signs lease at Brixton Capital's Del Mar Plaza retail, San Diego
1,168 SF mezzanine/café space; brand expansion (30+ locations since 2019) entering San Diego market
Retail tenant quality upgrade reflects neighborhood amenity lift and foot-traffic potential
stories.summary: Brixton Capital secured a lease with La La Land Café for 1,168 square feet of mezzanine and café space at Del Mar Plaza in San Diego. La La Land, which has grown to over 30 locations since its founding in 2019, is expanding into San Diego for the first time. The space replaces Pacifica Breeze Café. Construction start and opening dates are not yet determined.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily development impact. Retail tenant upgrading at a premier shopping center suggests sustained affluent-consumer spending in the Del Mar submarket, which indirectly supports demand for Class A apartments and mixed-use. However, the effect is localized to retail and does not signal material supply or capital shifts relevant to multifamily development timing.

stories.title: JLL Arranges Sale of Two Twin Cities Seniors Housing Properties
stories.excerpt: JLL has arranged the sale of Boulder Ponds Senior Living and Round Lake Senior Living, a 216-unit portfolio of seniors housing communities located in Lake Elmo and Arden Hills, Minnesota. JLL’s Seniors Housing Capital Markets team represented the seller, Trident Development, in the transaction and secured the buyer, LTC Properties, Inc. Lifespark will remain the operator of both communities. Developed by Trident Development, the portfolio comprises two purpose-built communities strategically located within the Twin Cities submarkets. Both communities offer independent living, assisted living and memory care services. Boulder Ponds Senior Living, completed in 2020, is a 95-unit community in Lake Elmo located at 192 Jade Trail N. The property has demonstrated strong operating performance and stability, maintaining approximately 98% occupancy. Round Lake Senior Living, which opened in 2023, is a 121-unit community in Arden Hills at 1740 Parkshore Dr. The community benefits from convenient access to major employment centers, retail amenities and healthcare services. The post JLL Arranges Sale of Two Twin Cities Seniors Housing Properties appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL arranges sale of 216-unit seniors housing portfolio (Boulder Ponds, Round Lake) to LTC Properties
Portfolio: Lake Elmo and Arden Hills, Minnesota; strong 98% occupancy at Boulder Ponds (opened 2020); Round Lake opened 2023
Lifespark remains operator; both communities offer independent, assisted, and memory care
stories.summary: JLL arranged the sale of Boulder Ponds Senior Living (95 units, Lake Elmo, opened 2020) and Round Lake Senior Living (121 units, Arden Hills, opened 2023) to LTC Properties, Inc. The 216-unit seniors housing portfolio was developed and sold by Trident Development. Boulder Ponds maintains approximately 98% occupancy and strong operating performance. Lifespark will remain the operator of both communities.
stories.impact: Limited direct bearing on market-rate multifamily. Seniors housing asset sales in Twin Cities reflect institutional appetite for stabilized, operator-managed age-restricted communities, but this signals demographic strength and long-term population aging that supports rental demand across all housing types in the Metro. Multifamily developers should note Twin Cities' stable labor market and in-migration trends, which have supported both market-rate and affordable absorption; continued strong seniors housing fundamentals validate the metro's demographic tailwinds.

stories.title: AI Wealth Management Platform Vise Grabs 12K SF at 50 Ninth Avenue
stories.excerpt: Artificial intelligence-powered wealth management platform Vise is moving from SoHo to 50 Ninth Avenue in the Meatpacking District, where it will quadruple its office space to 11,949 square feet. The space spans the second floor of several combined historic townhomes along the Ninth Avenue frontage and therefore has dramatic, over 20 foot-high pitched ceilings and an atrium outdoor garden. Rob Kluge and Brandon Charnas of Current Real Estate Advisors represented the tenant in the 10-year lease. Howard Hersch, Greg Conen, Jennifer Schreiber and Natalie Serio of Newmark represented the building owner, Tavros Capital, which will build out the space. The asking rent was $150 per square foot. Vise is an AI-driven wealth management platform for independent advisors founded by Samir Vasavada and Runik Mehrotra that launched in November 2019. It hosts over $100 billion in assets and the firm is reported to be valued at over $22 billion. It is currently located in 4,000 square feet of office space at 521 Broadway in SoHo. In searching for new digs, Vise was focused on upgrading both its office and culture. “We worked with ownership on a creative solution whereby the ground-floor retailer, Jen Rubio’s fashion company — now known as Elsa, which was then negotiating their deal — would expand upstairs and take roughly another 4,000 to 5,000 square feet on the West 14th Street side of the floor,” Charnas said. “That allowed us to create a space for Vise that fit both their program and their budget.” “We worked through multiple iterations with ownership and the architect to take what had been one larger floor and create the right long-term home for Vise,” added Kluge. The resulting space primarily overlooks Ninth Avenue and sits directly across from the Apple store, with dramatic vaulted ceilings, tons of light and a build-out being designed specifically around Vise’s needs and specifications. bullets: Vise (AI wealth mgmt platform, $22B valuation, $100B AUM) expands NYC footprint: SoHo to Meatpacking
11,949 SF lease at 50 Ninth Avenue (2nd floor); 10-year term; quadruples space from 4K SF
Tenant expansion reflects fintech/digital asset class strength and Manhattan office demand at premium rents ($150/SF)
stories.summary: Vise, an AI-powered wealth management platform valued at $22 billion and managing over $100 billion in assets, is relocating from SoHo to 50 Ninth Avenue in the Meatpacking District. The firm will quadruple its office footprint from 4,000 to 11,949 square feet under a 10-year lease at $150 per square foot. Current Real Estate Advisors represented the tenant; Newmark represented the landlord, Tavros Capital.
stories.impact: Fintech and digital-asset-class tenant growth in Meatpacking District (and broader Manhattan) indicates sustained high-wage job concentration and ecosystem strength in NYC, supporting rental demand for Class A apartments and luxury residential near major office clusters. Vise's footprint expansion signals confidence in NYC's talent pool and premium office market; multifamily developers near transit and office anchors (e.g., Hudson Yards, Meatpacking, Soho) should expect continued rental demand from white-collar workers in tech and finance.

stories.title: SME Capital Forced to Hand Over Hudson Yards Condo Building to Residents
stories.excerpt: Private investment firm SME Capital Ventures is handing ownership of 441 West 37th Street to the condominium board after an investigation by the New York Attorney General’s office. SME acquired the building out of foreclosure in 2023. It then failed to pay bills related to the Hudson Yards property and neglected safety violations, leading to a settlement to pay $700,000, according to Attorney General Letitia James. Built in 2020 by Levi Balkany, the nine-unit building went into foreclosure in 2023. SME never reported to the state that it was the winning bidder in the auction and never acknowledged that it owned the building, leaving residents to pick up the tab for things like a new $15,824 certificate of occupancy, according to the AG. Some of the units were rented out while awaiting buyers, including 35 formerly homeless people who were ousted around the time SME took control of the building, according to The Real Deal. “Private equity firms do not get to pick and choose which laws apply to them,” James said in a statement. “When this company took control of a Manhattan condo building, it took on real legal responsibilities to the homeowners who lived there. For two years, SME Capital dodged those duties while still collecting rent checks. My office will keep holding these firms accountable when they put profits over New Yorkers’ safety.” Balkany could not be reached for comment. bullets: SME Capital Ventures forced to surrender 441 West 37th Street (Hudson Yards) 9-unit condo to board
Private equity firm acquired out of foreclosure (2023), failed to pay bills, ignored safety violations; $700K settlement
Regulatory intervention and condo ownership conflict; developer accountability and investor-operator governance risk
stories.summary: Private investment firm SME Capital Ventures is surrendering ownership of 441 West 37th Street, a nine-unit condominium building in Hudson Yards, to the condominium board following an investigation by New York Attorney General Letitia James. SME acquired the building at foreclosure in 2023 but failed to pay bills and address safety violations. The settlement includes a $700,000 payment. The building was originally developed by Levi Balkany in 2020.
stories.impact: Regulatory and reputational risk for institutional residential investors and foreclosure acquirers in NYC. The enforcement action signals heightened AG scrutiny of private equity and institutional buyer conduct in residential assets, particularly condo buildings and small multifamily properties. Developers should be aware that distressed-asset acquisitions or condo conversions carry heightened governance and compliance risk under NY law; partnerships with experienced operators and robust legal/compliance frameworks are now table-stakes to avoid AG enforcement and loss of asset control.

stories.title: Sisters of the Visitation Monastery Sells to Integritas Capital for $42M
stories.excerpt: A 170-year-old monastery in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, has sold for $42.25 million. The Sisters of the Visitation’s 7.5-acre campus at 8902 Ridge Boulevard — a campus behind 30-foot stone walls, with a monastery, chapel and school — was bought by a group of Brooklyn-based developers and investors with a history of large residential projects, including leaders of Integritas Capital and Heights Advisors. A petition by the Catholic religious order to sell its real estate was approved by the office of the New York State Attorney General on Monday. Nonprofits are required by New York law to obtain approval when it sells all or most of its assets. The buyer entity, 1137 91 LLC, is led by Brooklyn real estate investor Stephen Palmese, founder of private equity platform Integritas Capital (and a former vice chair at JLL). Passive investors included Rachel Foster, founder and president of Brooklyn housing developer Heights Advisors, alongside the developer’s director, Scott Geddes, as well as Daniel Kodsi and Matthew Kodsi . The longtime professional partners are planning a resort-residential tower in Fort Lauderdale, according to The Real Deal. Palmese’s Integritas is also the lender behind a forthcoming 27-story church-to-residential conversion in Brooklyn’s Fort Greene. The cohort of buyers suggests the historic property’s likely fate as a major mixed-used or residential development. The Visitation Sisters entered into an initial contract in late April, according to the filing, but the school and monastery have been shuttered since 2024, after their numbers dropped too low to sustain full ministry. The Visitation Sisters, formally the Order of the Visitation of Holy Mary, were a French order founded in 1610. Their presence in Brooklyn dates back to 1855. The sellers expect net proceeds of $40.9 million, according to the filing, which will be held in escrow under an approved dissolution and distribution of assets plan. bullets: Sisters of the Visitation Monastery, Bay Ridge Brooklyn, sells 7.5-acre campus to Integritas Capital for $42.25M
Buyer: 1137 91 LLC led by Stephen Palmese (Integritas Capital, ex-JLL); passive investors include Heights Advisors
Large-scale institutional land play; 170-year-old nonprofit real estate conversion signals development pipeline opportunity
stories.summary: The Sisters of the Visitation Monastery sold its 7.5-acre campus at 8902 Ridge Boulevard in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, to a group of Brooklyn-based developers and investors led by Stephen Palmese (founder of Integritas Capital and former JLL vice chair) for $42.25 million. The deal includes passive investment from Rachel Foster (Heights Advisors) and Daniel and Matthew Kodsi. The campus, situated behind 30-foot stone walls and comprising a monastery, chapel, and school, required approval from the NY State Attorney General.
stories.impact: Major institutional land acquisition in Bay Ridge signals developer appetite for large, entitled or easily-entitleable sites in Brooklyn submarkets outside Crown Heights and Williamsburg. The deal price ($42.25M for 7.5 acres ≈ $2.52M/acre) and buyer profile (experienced Brooklyn residential developers) suggests a near-term multifamily development or mixed-use master-plan is likely. Competitors should monitor Bay Ridge zoning and entitlement trends; the submarket could become a secondary growth corridor as waterfront and central Brooklyn sites become scarce and expensive. First-mover advantage exists for developers with aligned community and agency relationships.

stories.title: Benefit Street Partners Provides $103M Bridge Debt for Texas Multifamily Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Vantage Communities has secured $103 million in bridge debt to refinance a three-property, 864-unit multifamily portfolio in three cities in Texas, Commercial Observer can first report. Benefit Street Partners provided the debt, which will finance the property toward full stabilization and is structured as a floating-rate, interest-only bridge loan with a three-year term. Greystone Capital Advisors‘ Drew Fletcher, Bryan Grover, Jesse Kopecky and Cameron Behr arranged the transaction. “Benefit Street Partners recognized the quality of the sponsorship, the assets, and the long-term fundamentals supporting these dynamic Central Texas markets,” said Fletcher. The three assets are split among Vantage at Hutto — a 288-unit complex located at 1051 North Farm to Market 1660 in Hutto, Tex., just outside of Austin; Vantage at McKinney Falls — a 288-unit complex located at 7900 McKinney Falls Parkway in suburban Austin, Tex.; and Vantage at Fair Oaks — a 288-unit complex located at 9135 Dietz Elkhorn Road in Boerne, Tex. outside of San Antonio. All three assets opened in either 2023 or 2024 and feature amenities such as resident clubhouses, fitness centers and resort-style swimming pools. “We were pleased to structure a financing solution that met our clients’ objectives while leveraging the strength of this high-quality, recently delivered portfolio,” added Fletcher in a statement. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Vantage Communities secures $103M floating-rate bridge debt (Benefit Street Partners) for 864-unit TX portfolio
Three assets: Hutto (288u), McKinney Falls/Austin (288u), Fair Oaks/Boerne (288u); 3-year term, interest-only
Central Texas market fundamentals support bridge capital; sponsor quality and submarket growth drive lender confidence
stories.summary: Vantage Communities secured $103 million in floating-rate bridge debt from Benefit Street Partners to refinance a three-property, 864-unit multifamily portfolio across Hutto, McKinney Falls (Austin), and Fair Oaks (Boerne), Texas. The loan is structured as interest-only with a three-year term. Greystone Capital Advisors arranged the transaction. The deal reflects lender confidence in the quality of the sponsor, the assets, and long-term fundamentals in Central Texas markets.
stories.impact: Bridge lending availability and favorable terms for stabilized multifamily in Central Texas signal strong capital-markets confidence in Austin metro and secondary-tier Texas markets (Boerne, Hutto). Strong sponsor reputation and portfolio scale are de-risking floating-rate exposure; the 3-year term reflects exit flexibility via permanent financing or sale. Multifamily developers in Central Texas should view this as validation of market fundamentals and sponsor quality as key underwriting levers. Compete on operational excellence and sponsor track record; markets themselves are competitive and supply-constrained, favoring experienced operators with proven asset management and exit optionality.
